task: buy a specific amount of a stock or crypto in a retail app (Robinhood, Coinbase, Fidelity, Cash App): search the ticker, enter a dollar amount or share count, review the order (price, fees), place it, and see the filled or pending confirmation; complete when the order confirmation is on screen. Surface pinned: a retail brokerage or crypto app or website. Variants: trading-strategy and technical-analysis content, price-prediction videos, and day-trading courses do not belong.

tree.label: Trade on an investing app
tree.note: do 1. 2 fires wherever the platform puts the wall: before the first buy (yeKU), inside the first buy (Wopd), only at send (DZKH), once per ramp even twice in one session (lBbZ). 3.1 every session; the rest of 3 as the rails demand. repeat 4 until an asset settles - 4.8 ends an orbit without a trade. then 5 and 6 as a pair, once per trade: four keepers run the pair twice, buy then sell (DZKH, eVJg, ZWfJ, lBbZ), and ten keepers run 5 without ever reaching 5.11. 7 when the holdings leave the platform (O1Ka, fDjD, lBbZ). 8 and 9 stand apart from any single trade and take over whole stretches of a session (w-mD, jH1r).

children.note: 1.1 then 1.7 - most keepers arrive signed in and 1.2 to 1.6 never fire. 1.2 to 1.5 on a first run (yeKU walks all of it; frXh chooses among managed tiers first). 1.6 recurs when a session lapses mid-task (yeKU signs back in after the 3-day wait). 1.8 swaps the whole session onto simulated money (JAFQ).

questions.question: Does the offer's fine print change what it actually pays?
questions.why: The prominent marketing offer of getting up to $200 in stock is contradicted by fine print stating that 99% of rewards are only worth $5.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the transparency needed to accurately evaluate if participating in the promotional referral offer is actually worth their time.
questions.check: What does the promotion's headline offer, and what do its stated terms or fine print say?
questions.say_example: About that <$5 to $200> offer. The fine print says <99 in 100 get the $5>. Count on <$5>.

questions.question: Do you want to claim your pending free stock reward?
questions.why: The screen displays a notification that a free stock for inviting a friend is ready to be claimed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to claim promotional rewards if the agent ignores them to focus strictly on the requested purchase.
questions.check: Does the page show a pending reward to claim?
questions.say_example: Free stock waiting to claim - left alone, say the word

questions.question: What specific stock were you awarded and what is its current value?
questions.why: The screen displays a congratulatory message confirming the exact ticker and dollar value of the awarded share.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means missing out on the immediate knowledge of which specific stock was awarded and its exact monetary value.
questions.check: What stock and value does the award screen state?
questions.say_example: You got <one share of Sony>, worth <$9.72>. It's in the account.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether to spend your time taking a quiz for free crypto rather than just paying for it.
questions.check: What earn-instead-of-buy options does the page show?

questions.question: Did the bonus land at the amount the offer stated?
questions.why: The initial screen offered $1 of ZRX for completing the lesson, so it is important to verify the success screen confirms exactly $1 was earned.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If the agent fails to verify this, you might complete the lesson but receive a different reward amount than what was promised.
questions.check: What amount did the offer state, and what amount does the completion or balance screen state was credited?
